title: Cyclospora cases climb to 147 in Mass., but officials say season remains within historical range
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Massachusetts reports 147 cyclospora cases from May 1 to August 1, linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce.
No large outbreaks are evident, though small clusters of illness are tied to recalled Taylor Farms lettuce.
Cyclospora parasite symptoms include diarrhea and weight loss, and are treatable with antibiotics; no deaths reported in Massachusetts.

title: Tow truck driver charged with motor vehicle homicide, police say he hit ‘highly visible’ pedestrian in Worcester
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Andrew Peperato, 52, is charged with motor vehicle homicide for allegedly hitting Van Thi Khanh Doan in Worcester.
Doan was struck in a marked crosswalk while Peperato was reportedly using his cellphone on June 10.
Peperato faces multiple charges, including negligent operation and improper turning; arraignment set for September 17.

title: Does Christian Gonzalez’ contract stalemate make Drake Maye think about his own Patriots future?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Christian Gonzalez's contract stalemate remains unresolved, despite an offer to make him the highest-paid cornerback.
Patriots quarterback Drake Maye will be eligible for contract extension after 2026, potentially earning close to $500 million.
Maye respects Gonzalez's participation in training camp despite contract issues, focusing on improving his own game.

title: 18-year-old uses ‘grit and determination’ to help with own rescue from Mount Washington
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: Andrew Nelson, 18, from Topsfield, Mass., injured his leg while hiking on Mount Washington's Tuckerman Ravine Trail.
Despite his injury, Nelson used sheer grit to crawl and hop three-tenths of a mile toward the summit for rescue.
Rescue crews reached Nelson near the summit, applied a splint, and transported him in a litter to safety.

title: Woman sues Court TV over release of her name in Irish firefighter rape case
author: Beth Treffeisen
bullets: Jane Doe is suing Court TV for $2.8 million, alleging the network disclosed her identity during a rape retrial.
The lawsuit claims Court TV displayed her name in a live broadcast and on social media, leading to online harassment.
The woman alleges the disclosure has worsened her mental health and seeks accountability for violating her privacy rights.

title: Healey signs sweeping law to restrict ICE
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts Governor Maura Healey signed the PROTECT Act to limit ICE actions in schools, hospitals, and courthouses.
The law allows parents to pre-arrange guardianship for their children in case of deportation and restricts warrantless arrests.
The PROTECT Act, effective immediately, expands legal protections for immigrants and establishes a new state civil rights claim.

title: Here’s how Mass. hospitals fared in the latest U.S. News rankings
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Brigham and Women's and Massachusetts General Hospital tied for first in Massachusetts in U.S. News rankings.
Both hospitals were named to the nationwide honor roll, which includes 20 top hospitals for excellence.
Dana-Farber Brigham Cancer Center ranked third nationally for cancer care specialization.

title: Stefon Diggs reportedly ‘set to sign’ with Commanders on one-year deal
author: Hayden Bird
bullets: Stefon Diggs is reportedly signing a one-year deal with the Washington Commanders, worth up to $12 million.
Diggs helped the Patriots reach the Super Bowl with 85 catches for 1,013 yards in 2025.
Patriots parted ways with Diggs after acquiring receiver A.J. Brown from the Eagles on June 1.

title: Patriots teammates believe Will Campbell is ready for Year 2 jump
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Will Campbell shows improvement in Patriots training camp, impressing teammates like Dre'Mont Jones and quarterback Drake Maye.
Campbell, recovering from a torn MCL, endured difficult moments in 2025, including 14 pressures in Super Bowl LX.
New England's offensive staff believes Campbell will make significant strides going into the 2026 NFL season.

title: Snag one-way fares for as low as $54 during JetBlue’s fall travel flash sale
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: JetBlue launched a 48-hour fall travel flash sale with one-way domestic fares starting at $54.
The sale ends Thursday at 11:59 p.m. EDT, valid for travel between September 9 and November 18.
Promotional fares include Boston to Presque Isle from $59 and London-Heathrow from $299.
